items.stem: Before executing a model-generated SQL query against BigQuery, the safest practice is to:

options.text: Validate it and run read-only with a cost/byte cap
options.rationale: Correct: validation and read-only limits prevent damaging or runaway queries.

options.text: Run it with full write access for flexibility
options.rationale: Write access lets a bad query modify data.

options.text: Trust it because the model produced valid syntax
options.rationale: Valid syntax does not mean the query is safe or correct.

options.text: Remove all quota limits to avoid interruptions
options.rationale: Removing limits risks a very expensive query.

items.explanation: Correct: validation and read-only limits prevent damaging or runaway queries.

items.stem: Why define metrics in a semantic layer rather than in each generated query?

options.text: To give one consistent, trusted definition for every answer
options.rationale: Correct: a shared semantic layer keeps metrics consistent and trustworthy.

options.text: To make queries run without BigQuery

options.rationale: A semantic layer does not replace access control.

options.text: To stop users from asking questions
options.rationale: The goal is to enable trustworthy questions, not block them.

items.explanation: Correct: a shared semantic layer keeps metrics consistent and trustworthy.

items.stem: Which TWO keep a conversational-analytics answer trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Ground the narrative in the actual query results
options.rationale: Correct: grounding ties the words to real returned figures.

options.text: State clearly when the data cannot answer the question
options.rationale: Correct: honest refusal prevents fabricated answers.

options.text: Hide the underlying SQL from reviewers

items.explanation: Correct: grounding in results and honest refusal both keep answers trustworthy.
